title: Alvarez: the will is passive to the premotion, active in its act
source_text: XLIX. Inde vero colligit istud Dei auxilium, voluntatis creatae actioni praevium, produci in illa effective a solo Deo, & nullo modo dependere efficienter ab influxu voluntatis ipsius: adeoque voluntatem in ordine ad illud praevium auxilium Dei se habere passive: quamvis eadem voluntas se habeat active & libere, in ordine ad actum liberum, ad quem praevio illo auxilio movetur. Disputationis modo citatae numero sexto.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. Thence however he gathers that that help of God, prior to the action of the created will, is produced in it effectively by God alone, and in no way depends efficiently on the influx of the will itself: and so that the will in order to that prior help of God holds itself passively: although the same will holds itself actively and freely, in order to the free act, to which it is moved by that prior help. Of the disputation just cited number sixth.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIX. From this he infers that this aid of God, which precedes the created will's action, is produced in the will effectively by God alone and in no way depends efficiently on any influence of the will itself. So with respect to that prior aid of God the will is passive, although the same will is active and free with respect to the free act to which that prior aid moves it. The disputation just cited, section 6.

choices.english: is passive ... is active (literal pass: holds itself passively/actively)
choices.why: The scholastic 'se habere' idiom rendered by the plain verb.

bible_refs: Diego Alvarez OP, De auxiliis divinae gratiae et humani arbitrii viribus (Rome, 1610), book 3, disputations 18-19.
